# Context menu misbehaves when right-clicked again while it is already open

## Bug report

I am wrapping an element with a context menu. When the menu is already open and I
right-click the element again in a different place, it does not respond the way I
would expect. The recording below shows what happens on that second right-click.

![Context menu on a second right-click while it is already open](/app/.harbor_assets/bug.gif)

# Radix Primitives

Radix Primitives is for building high-quality, accessible design systems and web apps.

## Architecture

This project is a monorepo managed with [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/). It uses the following tools:

- [vitest](https://vitest.dev/) for unit testing
- [storybook](https://storybook.js.org/) for component documentation
- [cypress](https://www.cypress.io/) for end-to-end testing
- [changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) for versioning and publishing
- [oxlint](https://github.com/oxlint-dev/oxlint) for linting
- [oxfmt](https://github.com/oxlint-dev/oxfmt) for formatting

## Tech Constraints

- **pnpm** only
- **TypeScript** only (local scripts can use JavaScript with `// @ts-check` and type annotations)

## Commit Conventions

[Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) — release-please auto-generates changelog. Use `!` suffix for breaking changes (e.g., `feat!:`).

## Commands

```bash
pnpm lint         # Lint the project
pnpm format       # Format the project
pnpm types:check  # Type check the project
pnpm test         # Run tests
pnpm build        # Build the project
```

## Adding a new package

Most packages are React-specific and live in a directory that matches the convention `packages/react/{package-id}`. For example, `@radix-ui/react-accordion` lives in `packages/react/accordion`.

New packages should follow the same general folder structure as existing packages:

```
packages/react/
  - {package-id}/
    - src/
      - {package-id}.tsx
      - index.ts
    - CHANGELOG.md
    - package.json
    - README.md
    - tsconfig.json
```

Reference other packages and copy their `package.json`, `README.md`, and `tsconfig.json` structure for new packages. devDependencies and peerDependencies should use consistent version ranges across the repo.

## Code conventions

- [ ] Prefer braces for control flow statements (if, for, while, etc.) over the `one-liner` syntax
- [ ] Prefer braces for switch cases
- [ ] Explicitly check `never` cases for more exhaustive type checking (eg. `value satisfies never`)
- [ ] Prefer clear variable/function names over abbreviations (long descriptive names are good if they clarify the intent)

## Pre-commit checklist

- [ ] Run `pnpm lint --fix` to handle auto-fixable linting errors, then fix any remaining linting errors
- [ ] Run `pnpm format`

## PR checklist

- [ ] `pnpm format:check` passes
- [ ] `pnpm lint` passes
- [ ] `pnpm test` passes
- [ ] `pnpm types:check` passes
- [ ] Conventional Commit message format used (`feat:`, `fix:`, `feat!:` for breaking)

The fix is minimal, well-tested, and confirmed to resolve the exact bug described.

## Summary

**Root cause:** `ContextMenuTrigger`'s `onContextMenu` handler unconditionally called `context.onOpenChange(true)` on every right-click. When the menu was already open, this was a no-op under `useControllableState` (setting state to its current value doesn't trigger a re-render), so the menu's underlying `Menu.Content`/`Popper.Content` never remounted or re-anchored — it just stayed fixed at its original position and ignored the new click coordinates. This matched the GIF: the custom menu opened once and then stopped responding to further right-clicks, letting the native browser context menu show through since nothing in React ever changed to warrant a new `preventDefault()`-driven remount at the new point. (Interestingly, the touch/pen long-press path already had explicit close-then-reopen logic — the mouse path was simply missing the equivalent.)

**Fix** (`packages/react/context-menu/src/context-menu.tsx`): when `onContextMenu` fires while the menu is already open, first close it via `flushSync(() => context.onOpenChange(false))` — forcing the state change to actually commit — before reopening at the new point. A plain synchronous `onOpenChange(false)` immediately followed by `onOpenChange(true)` in the same handler gets batched by React into a no-op, which I verified experimentally before landing on `flushSync` as the correct approach (already used elsewhere in the repo, e.g. `primitive.tsx`, `one-time-password-field.tsx`).

**Test added** (`context-menu.test.tsx`): a regression test that right-clicks at one point, then a different point while open, and asserts the menu content actually remounts (proving re-anchoring, not just an eventually-self-correcting position via floating-ui's `ResizeObserver`-driven auto-update, which I found can mask this bug in jsdom if you only assert on the final CSS transform).
